catalog_quote: 本稿では必要に応じて平板型アクセントを0、下降型アクセントを⑴で表す。東京方言では下降の位置が弁別的であり、拍数が増えるとアクセントの型もｎ＋１（ｎ音節の語にはｎ＋１のアクセント型がある）のように増加するが、首里方言ではアクセントの位置は決まっており非弁別的である。この点、同じく２型の語声調方言といわれる鹿児島方言と似ている。異なるのは、鹿児島方言では下降型のアクセントが最後から２拍目であるのに対し、首里方言は最初から２拍目（ただし２拍語のときは１拍目）、また鹿児島方言の平板型は最後の拍が高いが、首里方言は通常、全部の拍が平らとされているなどの点である。なお、首里方言における下降型アクセントの占める割合は、東京方言や大阪方言のそれと比較すると極めて少なく、圧倒的多数の語が平板型アクセントである。 ... 首里方言は下降型と平板型の２型を区別する語声調方言であるので、（第２モーラの後に）ピッチの下降がある「荒儲けですか」と平板型「山田さんですか」を例文として使用した。

tone_statements.citation: 上野善道 (Uwano, Zendo). 2018. これまでの琉球方言アクセント研究とこれから [Accent research of Ryukyu dialects: past, present, and future] (特集 多様化する日本語研究の現在). 國學院雑誌 (Kokugakuin Zasshi) 119(11): 97-108.
tone_statements.quote: 首里方言が二型アクセント（ただし，長い複合語には末尾の１～２モーラの低くなる第３の型がある，との注記に注目） … その首里方言の音調に関し，（２）に要約した指摘がその「解説篇」にある … （２）⓪型と①型の二型で，すべての文節が平板型，下降型のいずれかに属するが，一部の複合語および種々の助詞や接尾形式の付いた形には，Ɂuukuba]a ⓪ … ’judoote]era]a ⓪（読んでいたのなら）など二次的な下降をもつものがある（4）。（p. 54）
tone_statements.translation: [Research in this period effectively begins with Hattori 1954 [1960], which states that] the Shuri dialect has a two-pattern accent (note, however, the remark that long compounds have a third pattern in which the final 1-2 moras become low) ... Concerning the pitch of the Shuri dialect, the observation summarised in (2) is in the [Okinawago jiten] commentary volume ... (2) Two patterns, type 0 and type 1; every phrase belongs to either the level (flat) type or the falling type, but some compounds and forms with various particles or suffixes attached have a secondary fall, e.g. Ɂuukuba]a (0) 'back tooth' ... 'judoote]era]a (0) 'if (you) had been reading' (p. 54).
tone_statements.locator: pp. 98-99, §1.2.1-§1.2.2 with example (2); author's reanalysis p. 103 §2.1; notes (4), (7) p. 107
tone_statements.summary: Two-pattern word accent (flat vs falling; Hattori 1954, Okinawago jiten 1963) with secondary falls in some compounds; the author suggests it may hide a register-plus-kernel system of 4+ patterns.

tone_statements.quote: ２、アクセント 那覇方言のアクセントについて、戦前には大湾政和（1937）、金城朝永（1944）の仕事があり … 比嘉論文の記述は、核と低高のはじめをあらわす２種の計３種の概念でもって記述している。小論においては「と￢の２種の概念で記述する。 … ともあれ、結果は平板・尾高・中高・頭高型という術語が出たり、アクセントの山を意識していると思われるところがあったりで、音韻的処理は、後退している感があるかもしれない。 … 以下、６拍までの型と形の例、及び語例をあげる。 ２．１，平板型 ○○ ○○○ … /○○/ hana〈鼻〉、kubi〈首〉、kii〈毛〉、mii〈実〉 … ２．２，尾高型 ○○「 ○○「○ … /○○「/ … ʔami〈雨〉、kata〈肩〉 … ２．３，中高型 ○「○￢○○ … ２．４，頭高型 … /○○￢/
tone_statements.translation: 2. Accent. On the accent of the Naha dialect there is pre-war work by Owan Seiwa (1937) and Kinjo Choei (1944) ... Higa's paper describes it with three concepts in all: the kernel plus two marking the onset of low and of high. This paper describes it with two concepts, 「 [rise] and ￢ [fall]. ... In any case the result is that terms such as level (heiban), final-high (odaka), mid-high (nakadaka) and initial-high (atamadaka) type appear, and there are places where an accent peak seems to be assumed, so the phonological treatment may have regressed ... Below I give the types and shapes up to six morae with word examples. 2.1 Level type /○○/ hana 'nose', kubi 'neck', kii 'hair', mii 'fruit' ... 2.2 Final-high type /○○「/ ʔami 'rain', kata 'shoulder' ... 2.3 Mid-high type ... 2.4 Initial-high type /○○￢/
tone_statements.locator: pp.11-14, section 2、アクセント (2.1 平板型 - 2.4 頭高型; two-mora neutralisation statement p.14 §2.5)
tone_statements.summary: Old-Naha Okinawan word accent: high/low mora patterns marked by a rise and a fall, giving level, final-high, mid-high and initial-high types (to 6 morae); 2-mora words contrast only before a particle.

tone_statements.citation: 中本正智 (Nakamoto, Masachie). 1960. 沖縄南部の1・2音節語のアクセント [Accentuation of one- and two-syllable words in southern Okinawa]. 国語学 (Kokugogaku) 41 (特輯: 琉球), 39-50. Tokyo: 国語学会.
tone_statements.quote: 2.4 アクセント素 この方言のアクセントはつぎのように弁別できる.(1)下り核があるかないか,(2)あればどこにあるか.そこで表記は音韻記号を用いる.アクセントは┐によって核の場所を表記する.┐のないものは,核のないことを表わす. … 知念村・玉城村・佐敷村がほとんどC3〔●○・●○△(第一・二類),○○・○○△(第三類)〕で統一されており,これは沖縄南部でもっとも大きなグループをなす.さらに,かつて王城のあった首里は,この型にもっとも近いC4〔●○,●●△(第一・二類),○○・○○△(第三類)〕になっており,周囲への広がりがあまりない.
tone_statements.translation: 2.4 Accentemes. The accent of this dialect can be distinguished as follows: (1) whether or not there is a falling kernel, (2) if so, where it is. ... the accent is written with ┐ marking the place of the kernel; forms without ┐ have no kernel. ... Chinen, Tamagusuku and Sashiki are almost uniformly C3 [●○/●○△ (classes 1-2), ○○/○○△ (class 3)], the largest group in southern Okinawa; Shuri, the former royal seat, has the closest type, C4 [●○, ●●△ (classes 1-2), ○○/○○△ (class 3)], with little spread to its surroundings.
tone_statements.locator: Kokugogaku 41: section 2.4 'アクセント素' (Ou dialect) and section 3 (areal types; Shuri = C4), pp. 39-50
tone_statements.summary: Southern Okinawan (Ou/Tamagusuku) lexical pitch accent defined by presence and position of a falling kernel only; across southern Okinawa 2-syllable nouns split classes 1-2 (falling) vs class 3 (level), Shuri being areal type 'C4'.

tone_statements.citation: 比嘉政夫 (Higa, Masao). 1960. 旧那覇市垣花方言のアクセント体系 [The accentual system of Kakihana dialect in older Naha City]. 国語学 (Kokugogaku / Studies in the Japanese Language) 41 (特輯: 琉球), 28-38. Tokyo: 国語学会.
tone_statements.quote: 3.1 この方言のアクセントの音韻的型(以後,これをたんに型とよび,「音声的型」と区別する)の弁別的特徴は,(1)アクセント核(以後これをたんに核という)があるかないか.(2)あればどのモーラにあるか.(3)高くはじまるか低くはじまるか.という点にある.なお,核は原則として,第一モーラと最後から二番目のモーラをのぞき,どのモーラの上にも位置しうる. … 3.2 …この方言のアクセントの非弁別的特徴についてのべる.(1)二モーラからなる型は,すべて音声的には中平型[├○○]である.
tone_statements.translation: 3.1 The distinctive features of the phonological accent patterns of this dialect (hereafter simply 'patterns', as opposed to 'phonetic patterns') are: (1) whether or not there is an accent kernel (hereafter simply 'kernel'); (2) if there is one, on which mora it lies; (3) whether the word begins high or low. As a rule the kernel may lie on any mora except the first and the second from the end. ... 3.2 ... the non-distinctive features of this dialect's accent: (1) all two-mora patterns are phonetically mid-level [├○○].
tone_statements.locator: Kokugogaku 41, section 3 'アクセント', 3.1-3.2 (pp. 30-31 of pp. 28-38)
tone_statements.summary: Old-Naha (Kakihana) word-pitch system analysed as lexical pitch accent: kernel (fall) present/absent, kernel mora, and H vs L onset register; kernel barred from 1st and penultimate mora; 2-mora words neutralised to level; kernel shifts leftward before monomoraic particles.

tone_statements.citation: 金田一春彦 (Kindaichi, Haruhiko). 1960. アクセントから見た琉球語諸方言の系統 [The genealogy of the Ryukyuan dialects as seen from accent]. 東京外国語大学論集 (Area and Culture Studies, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies) 7: 59-80. doi:10.15026/23275, hdl:10108/23275.

tone_statements.translation: [Table 1] (32) (Okinawa) Shuri: classes 1-2 = HL ~ HH+low particle pattern; class 3 = HH ~ HH+high particle pattern; classes 4-5 = HH ~ HH+high particle / (long first syllable) HHH ~ HHH+high particle pattern; [group II] ... [Notes to Table 1] (32) Class 3 and classes 4-5 I recognise as the high-level pattern, from the observation I made of Mr. Sadoyama ... . The class 1-2 monosyllabic nouns of this dialect, when a particle is attached, are HL(particle low), unlike the class 1-2 disyllabic nouns. Or perhaps the disyllabic nouns too should be taken as HL-pattern, as Dr. Hirayama does. ... [II] Dialects that split (classes 1-2) : (classes 3-4-5). E.g. (1), (7), (10), (30)-(32), (34)-(36), (41) ...
tone_statements.locator: p. 62, 〔第1表〕 row (32) 首里; p. 64, 〔第1表〕の〔註〕(32) and classification box 〔II〕; cf. pr. p. 77 '(32)の首里は新里と全く同じ…'
tone_statements.summary: Two accent patterns on two-syllable nouns: classes 1-2 high-low (high-high + low particle) vs classes 3-5 high-level; grouped with the Ryukyuan dialects that split (1-2):(3-4-5).

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: both Japanese passages are verbatim in the Hosei-repository PDF we hold at the stated pages (p.176 and p.184-185), and the English supporting sentence is in the held ICPhS 2011 paper at p.1434. (2) The deciding source is a 2010 instrumental intonation study by the two specialists on Shuri prosody; its accent paragraph restates their own 2009 instrumental accent study and the NINJAL 1963 Okinawago jiten, both of which I downloaded now (Hosei repository; NINJAL repository, CC-BY) and both of which state the same system: two lexically assigned word-accent classes, flat (level throughout) vs falling (high up to mora 2, mora 1 only in bimoraic words, then low), locus fixed and non-distinctive. Nothing in any of the four sources describes a word-stress rule; the 1963 dictionary's remark that mora 1 of falling-type words is 'slightly stronger' is given as a property of the falling pi

sources.quote: p.65: '首里方言はいわゆる語声調方言（早田 1999）であり、平板型と下降型の２つのアクセント型をもつ。有核型、無核型と呼ばれることもある… 首里方言ではアクセントの位置は決まっており非弁別的である… 首里方言は最初から２拍目（ただし２拍語のときは１拍目）… 首里方言は通常、全部の拍が平らとされている'. p.66 (4.1): '下降型のアクセントを持つ語は、２拍語の場合には第１拍だけが高く第２拍は低い。３拍以上の下降型の語では、通常第２拍までが高く、以後の拍は終わりまで低く平らに…', followed by F0 measurements.

sources.citation: 国立国語研究所 (Kokuritsu Kokugo Kenkyūjo / NINJAL), ed. 1963 [9th printing 2001]. 沖縄語辞典 (Okinawago jiten / A dictionary of the Ryukyuan language: Shuri dialect). 国立国語研究所資料集 5. Tokyo: 大蔵省印刷局. 854 pp. doi:10.15084/00002266.
sources.quote: '首里方言のアクセントは平板型と下降型の二つに分かれる。… アクセントは単語ごとに定まっているが、アクセントの単位をなすものはいわゆる「文節」である。平板型のアクセントを持つ単語は、はじめ中程度のあるいはやや低い高さで始まり、終わりまで大体同じ高さが続く。… 下降型のアクセントを持つ単語は平板型の単語よりも高く始まり、かつ第1モーラは第2モーラ以下と比べてやや強く発音される。そして2モーラの単語の場合には第1モーラだけが高く、第2モーラは低い。3モーラ以上の下降型の単語では、通常第2モーラまでが高く、以下のモーラは低く終わりまで平らに続く。' (adds that in falling-type words mora 2 tends to be low too when it is a vowel-only mora or N, esp. in long vowels). Two lexical classes, pitch-defined, fixed fall locus — same system as coded; the 'slightly stronger' first mora is described as a concomitant of the falling (high-initial) type, not an independent stress rule

tone.translation: 2. Accent. On the accent of the Naha dialect there is pre-war work by Owan Seiwa (1937) and Kinjo Choei (1944) ... Higa's paper describes it with three concepts in all: the kernel plus two marking the onset of low and of high. This paper describes it with two concepts, 「 [rise] and ￢ [fall]. ... In any case the result is that terms such as level (heiban), final-high (odaka), mid-high (nakadaka) and initial-high (atamadaka) type appear, and there are places where an accent peak seems to be assumed, so the phonological treatment may have regressed ... Below I give the types and shapes up to six morae with word examples. 2.1 Level type /○○/ hana 'nose', kubi 'neck', kii 'hair', mii 'fruit' ... 2.2 Final-high type /○○「/ ʔami 'rain', kata 'shoulder' ... 2.3 Mid-high type ... 2.4 Initial-high type /○○￢/

tone.translation: 2.4 Accentemes. The accent of this dialect can be distinguished as follows: (1) whether or not there is a falling kernel, (2) if so, where it is. ... the accent is written with ┐ marking the place of the kernel; forms without ┐ have no kernel. ... Chinen, Tamagusuku and Sashiki are almost uniformly C3 [●○/●○△ (classes 1-2), ○○/○○△ (class 3)], the largest group in southern Okinawa; Shuri, the former royal seat, has the closest type, C4 [●○, ●●△ (classes 1-2), ○○/○○△ (class 3)], with little spread to its surroundings.
tone.summary: Southern Okinawan (Ou/Tamagusuku) lexical pitch accent defined by presence and position of a falling kernel only; across southern Okinawa 2-syllable nouns split classes 1-2 (falling) vs class 3 (level), Shuri being areal type 'C4'.

tone.translation: 3.1 The distinctive features of the phonological accent patterns of this dialect (hereafter simply 'patterns', as opposed to 'phonetic patterns') are: (1) whether or not there is an accent kernel (hereafter simply 'kernel'); (2) if there is one, on which mora it lies; (3) whether the word begins high or low. As a rule the kernel may lie on any mora except the first and the second from the end. ... 3.2 ... the non-distinctive features of this dialect's accent: (1) all two-mora patterns are phonetically mid-level [├○○].
tone.summary: Old-Naha (Kakihana) word-pitch system analysed as lexical pitch accent: kernel (fall) present/absent, kernel mora, and H vs L onset register; kernel barred from 1st and penultimate mora; 2-mora words neutralised to level; kernel shifts leftward before monomoraic particles.

tone.quote: 首里方言では,この｢板｣類と｢息｣類は,専らその第1音節の母音が長いか短いかによって区別されるものであって,それらのアクセソトは両者とも同じ型で出現する.(『沖縄語辞典』(1963:53)では,これらは全て｢平板型｣,すなわち｢はじめ中程度のあるいはやや低い高さで始まり,終わりまで大体同じ高さが続く｣型と記述されている.)
tone.locator: p.91, sec. 2.1 第1音節の母音の長さとアクセント型の規則的対応, paragraph above [表1], with [表3] p.93
tone.translation: In the Shuri dialect the 'ita' class and the 'iki' class are distinguished solely by whether the vowel of the first syllable is long or short, and as for their accent both appear with the same pattern. (In the Okinawago jiten (1963: 53) these are all described as 'heiban-gata' [level pattern], i.e. the pattern that 'begins at a mid or somewhat low pitch and continues at roughly the same height to the end'.)
